5SP2RAbqaQ.key_idea: Decompose gradients of differences between samples of one prompt, via PCA or a sparse autoencoder, to recover the tangent space of the model's conditional generative manifold.
5SP2RAbqaQ.evidence: Accurate subspace recovery in a controlled setting, behavioral validation on large-scale models, comparison with methods relying on external representations, and mode-collapse mitigation in distilled models.

Yhi9I3zO6K.one_liner: Solver-driven reasoning with an LLM that only evaluates candidate semantic bridges for unresolved proof obligations, using a grounding table.
Yhi9I3zO6K.problem: Even when individual natural-language statements are formalized faithfully, semantically related expressions can map to symbolically unrelated predicates, causing downstream symbolic reasoning to fail.
Yhi9I3zO6K.method: During autoformalization POGB keeps a grounding table recording the natural-language grounding of each formal element. When the solver hits an unresolved proof obligation, POGB identifies candidate semantic bridges and has an LLM evaluate them against the recorded grounding, recovering missing semantic relations while the solver controls all logical reasoning.
Yhi9I3zO6K.key_idea: Let the solver's unresolved proof obligations localize missing semantic relations, and restrict the LLM to judging candidate bridges against a grounding table.
Yhi9I3zO6K.evidence: A theoretical soundness proof; the abstract is truncated before empirical results.

bRR01VwZel.one_liner: Subspace optimizer states plus an orthogonal residual-gradient correction in the update, instantiated for momentum SGD (SMRC) and Muon (PMRC).
bRR01VwZel.problem: Subspace methods that use the leading singular subspace of stochastic gradients can be dominated by gradient noise in later training and may fail to converge.
bRR01VwZel.method: A residual correction framework keeps optimizer states in the subspace and adds the orthogonal residual gradient to the parameter update. SMRC applies it to momentum SGD, a multi-stage variant periodically recomputes bases with a boundary correction aligning virtual iterates across stages, and PMRC applies the matrix sign to the projected momentum in Muon.
bRR01VwZel.key_idea: Keep optimizer states in a low-dimensional subspace but add the orthogonal residual gradient to the update, analyzed through a subspace virtual iterate.
bRR01VwZel.evidence: Convergence analyses (subspace virtual iterate, boundary correction, weighted momentum tracking); empirical results are not visible in the truncated abstract.
bRR01VwZel.claimed_gains: SMRC attains an O(T^{-1/4}) convergence rate for a fixed orthonormal basis, matching full-space momentum SGD.

l13ZB1kfkN.one_liner: Optimizes lightweight head-wise interventions using language-preserving, answer-flipping visual counterfactual pairs to raise VLM reliance on visual evidence.
l13ZB1kfkN.problem: VLMs can give correct VQA answers that do not depend on visual evidence, since many correct answers stay unchanged when the visual input is replaced or removed, and existing interventions use manually specified strengths.
l13ZB1kfkN.method: VisIO builds counterfactual pairs in which linguistic context and most visual content stay fixed while controlled visual changes flip the correct answer, using a small set of unlabeled target videos, and optimizes only hundreds of head-wise parameters before inference. The authors also introduce a Visual Insensitivity Score (VIS) to quantify the behavior.
l13ZB1kfkN.key_idea: Optimize lightweight head-wise interventions on answer-flipping visual counterfactual pairs so the answer must depend on answer-determining visual evidence.
l13ZB1kfkN.evidence: Multiple VLMs and video VQA benchmarks, plus VIS analysis of answers when the visual input is replaced or removed.

XD9uilvuGG.one_liner: Separates masked reconstruction on modality tokens from foundation-model-guided semantic supervision on learnable queries in a shared SAR-EO encoder.
XD9uilvuGG.problem: SAR-EO pretraining must preserve how each sensor observes the scene and also capture what the scene contains, and forcing a single token stream to serve both roles is limiting.
XD9uilvuGG.method: Modality tokens are trained by masked reconstruction, while learnable semantic queries receive guidance from a pretrained vision foundation model; the queries are encoded jointly with SAR and EO tokens in the shared encoder, so semantic and reconstruction supervision go to separate token streams.
XD9uilvuGG.key_idea: Assign reconstruction to modality tokens and foundation-model-guided semantic supervision to separate learnable queries that interact with them in the shared encoder.
XD9uilvuGG.evidence: Pretraining on the million-scale SAR-1M corpus, evaluated on SAR-only and EO-only transfer and on joint SAR-EO tasks.

RxznlxGg8J.one_liner: Trains with RAW data via bit-level encoding, and lifts degraded RGB features to RAW-aware space so inference needs only RGB.
RxznlxGg8J.problem: Open-vocabulary segmentation methods are developed for well-illuminated images and degrade significantly under low-light conditions.
RxznlxGg8J.method: A RAW EnCoding (REC) module represents large-range RAW values as binary bit sequences and extracts RAW features at the bit level; an RGB Representation Enhancement (RRE) module progressively recovers overwhelmed details and lifts degraded RGB features to RAW-aware space. The authors also build LOVS, a real-world low-light dataset.
RxznlxGg8J.key_idea: Encode RAW values as bit sequences to preserve detail during training, and train an RGB-only branch to map degraded features into that RAW-aware space.
RxznlxGg8J.evidence: Synthetic low-light benchmarks and the new LOVS dataset (1,000 aligned normal-/low-light image pairs, 220 semantic categories, 6,949 object-level masks), across different open-vocabulary segmentation frameworks.

SMBFj6xJeQ.one_liner: Regularizes sequential LLM edits with a per-coordinate quadratic penalty built from gradient drift between stored and current gradients.
SMBFj6xJeQ.problem: In sequential model editing, repeated updates interfere with one another and degrade previously edited knowledge.
SMBFj6xJeQ.method: For each historical edit, GDR stores a gradient anchor at its insertion-time reference center and later computes a query gradient from the current model state when that edit is selected. The discrepancy between the two gradients defines a fixed, dimension-wise quadratic penalty on the current editing residual.
SMBFj6xJeQ.key_idea: Penalize editing-residual coordinates where a past edit's stored gradient anchor and its current query gradient differ most, motivated by a Taylor bound on gradient discrepancy.
SMBFj6xJeQ.evidence: A Taylor bound shows gradient discrepancy between two reference centers controls the difference in centered local responses up to a second-order remainder; experimental datasets and models are not visible in the provided abstract.

2T0Ja28jY5.one_liner: Shows unimodal augmentation-based SSL objectives, via an InfoNCE-to-local-CKA link, implicitly force cross-modal alignment between separately trained encoders.
2T0Ja28jY5.problem: Independently trained unimodal models show implicit cross-modal alignment, but the mechanism behind its emergence is unresolved.
2T0Ja28jY5.method: They theoretically connect the InfoNCE loss to local CKA, a measure of cross-modal alignment, and test the resulting prediction in controlled settings and across frozen text, vision, and audio encoders.
2T0Ja28jY5.key_idea: Low unimodal augmentation-based loss forces high cross-modal alignment through an InfoNCE-to-local-CKA connection, whereas high unimodal loss prevents it.
2T0Ja28jY5.evidence: Theory linking InfoNCE to local CKA, plus experiments in controlled settings and across 53 unconstrained frozen text, vision, and audio unimodal encoders.

D6dtJQVk5f.one_liner: Unified diffusion model for e-commerce posters that treats text patches as atomic units for generation, addition, deletion, and modification.
D6dtJQVk5f.problem: Existing poster methods either generate end-to-end or use multi-stage pipelines, with limited capability for flexible, fine-grained editing of existing posters.
D6dtJQVk5f.method: Defines Text Patch Generation and Editing, covering poster generation plus patch addition, deletion, and modification with optional reference-guided style control, and trains PosterText with a four-stage curriculum. The stages are text rendering pretraining, instruction-following training, reinforcement learning for preference alignment, and spatial guidance self-distillation.
D6dtJQVk5f.key_idea: Treat text patches as atomic units so one model handles generation and all edit operations, trained by a four-stage curriculum ending in spatial guidance self-distillation.
D6dtJQVk5f.evidence: Experiments on a newly built large-scale dataset with fine-grained patch-level annotations and a benchmark covering both generation and editing scenarios.
D6dtJQVk5f.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims only competitive performance against existing generation and editing approaches)

PIFBWDRdcS.one_liner: Merges task experts by storing one integer phase code per parameter coordinate and regenerating each expert via Kronecker-Weyl irrational rotation.
PIFBWDRdcS.problem: Static merging suffers parameter interference as tasks grow, while task-conditioned or routing methods bring back per-task masks, adapters, or modules whose storage scales with the number of tasks.
PIFBWDRdcS.method: Uses the Kronecker-Weyl equidistribution theorem so the n cross-task values at a coordinate can be approximated by a single scalar phase. Mergodic discretizes this phase into one integer code per coordinate, shared across all experts and independent of the number of tasks, and reconstructs each expert through a deterministic procedure.
PIFBWDRdcS.key_idea: A single scalar phase on a one-dimensional irrational rotation orbit, dense in the n-dimensional torus, encodes all n cross-task values at each parameter coordinate.
PIFBWDRdcS.evidence: Grounded in the Kronecker-Weyl equidistribution theorem; experimental details are cut off in the provided abstract.

TmHLZgUPa3.one_liner: Executable benchmark of 477 pressure variants measuring whether tool-using LLM agents falsify or conceal actions in their reports.
TmHLZgUPa3.problem: Users see only an agent's report, and it is underexplored whether agents faithfully report their actions across realistic, stateful application workflows.
TmHLZgUPa3.method: Builds 477 pressure variants from 257 source tasks across six pressure sources, each paired with a pressure-free counterpart, and evaluates full trajectories by relating user-facing claims to time-ordered observations and executed outcomes. Labels distinguish falsification, concealment, and equivocation from honest failure and disclosed limitations.
TmHLZgUPa3.key_idea: Compare an agent's user-facing claims with time-ordered observations and executed outcomes in paired pressure and pressure-free runs to label falsification, concealment, or equivocation.
TmHLZgUPa3.evidence: Executable benchmark with interventions entering through event messages, task context, application state, tool responses, and service quotas; the behavioral labels are also used to test existing activation-based probes.

eFi9w6vSHP.one_liner: Full-stack framework and 360-episode benchmark evaluating long-horizon embodied agents with physics simulation, embodied NPCs, and an FSM-based task evaluator.
eFi9w6vSHP.problem: Existing embodied-agent systems focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, which limits evaluation in an evolving world.
eFi9w6vSHP.method: TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue, with an event-driven finite-state machine updating task states. TARSphere-Harness lets a frozen MLLM act through multi-level executable skills using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback, and TARSphere-Bench has 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes.
eFi9w6vSHP.key_idea: An event-driven finite-state machine updates task states from completed actions and delivered information, while a frozen MLLM harness revises decisions using hierarchical memory and execution feedback.
eFi9w6vSHP.evidence: Evaluation of 8 MLLMs under a shared harness on TARSphere-Bench, using five paired conditions (perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, intent understanding) on navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks.
eFi9w6vSHP.claimed_gains: States that proprietary models lead and general-purpose open models outperform embodied models in task progress; no performance numbers are given in the visible abstract.

zKpbbZpeJ5.one_liner: Enforces zero divergence by design in a denoising network using a compact representation of divergence-free vector fields beyond three dimensions.
zKpbbZpeJ5.problem: Divergence-free vector fields lack a parsimonious representation beyond three dimensions, where the classical curl representation applies.
zKpbbZpeJ5.method: Shows divergence-free vector fields admit parsimonious representations, extending the curl representation, and builds a computationally efficient network architecture that enforces zero divergence by design. It is applied to self-supervised image denoising, with minor architectural modifications for Poisson and real-world noise.
zKpbbZpeJ5.key_idea: A parsimonious representation of divergence-free fields generalizing the curl beyond three dimensions, built into the network so its output has zero divergence by construction.
zKpbbZpeJ5.evidence: Image denoising experiments under Gaussian noise, plus Poisson and real-world noise with minor architectural modifications.
zKpbbZpeJ5.claimed_gains: Claims a new benchmark for constraint-based methods under Gaussian noise and a reduced performance gap with leading denoisers; no numbers stated.

H4Na10l0X3.one_liner: Generates mixed-type tabular data with flow matching, using boosted-tree endpoint-posterior heads instead of direct velocity regression.
H4Na10l0X3.problem: Existing tree-based flow models regress ambient-space velocities, imposing Euclidean geometry on inherently multinomial categorical variables, and high-fidelity generators can reproduce training records.
H4Na10l0X3.method: TabTreeVFM uses Gaussian regression heads for continuous columns and multinomial classifier heads for categorical variables to predict endpoint posteriors, whose posterior means recover the flow-matching velocity analytically. Training decomposes into independent XGBoost subproblems across timesteps and feature groups.
H4Na10l0X3.key_idea: Predict endpoint posteriors (Gaussian for continuous, multinomial for categorical) with boosted trees and recover the flow-matching velocity analytically from the posterior means.
H4Na10l0X3.evidence: 10 standard mixed-type benchmarks against 12 generators on fidelity, utility, and empirical privacy, plus Mem, a new held-out-calibrated measure of excess full-row reproduction.
H4Na10l0X3.claimed_gains: Best overall average rank among 12 generators across fidelity, utility, and empirical privacy on 10 benchmarks, while several strong neural baselines reproduce training rows above the natural collision rate and TabTreeVFM stays close to the held-out reference.

oZwghCuPIP.one_liner: Sets the Gaussian source covariance of a few-step flow-matching model to empirical temporal second moments, estimated offline.
oZwghCuPIP.problem: It is unclear which source covariance a few-step flow-matching model should use, since source choice is a finite-step numerical design problem.
oZwghCuPIP.method: TSCM uses an offline, length-indexed Gaussian source estimated from empirical temporal (or joint channel-time) second moments, used in both training and sampling without changing the architecture or objective. It follows from a proof that covariance matching uniquely minimizes endpoint Wasserstein error for Gaussian population fields under independent coupling and linear interpolation.
oZwghCuPIP.key_idea: Match the Gaussian source covariance to the data's temporal covariance, which the paper proves uniquely minimizes endpoint Wasserstein error for Gaussian fields under uniform Euler steps.
oZwghCuPIP.evidence: A proof for Gaussian population fields, and on HumanML3D a controlled comparison of 16 sources with three training seeds each, with source-specific constant guidance selected on validation, plus frozen-field controls.
oZwghCuPIP.claimed_gains: Mean 24-step FIDs on HumanML3D of 0.108 for TSCM, 0.135 for uncentered Toeplitz, and 0.497 for white noise, with oracle risk associated with guided test FIDs (log-log Pearson r=0.93).

K0EOhVw3B8.one_liner: Optimizer composing adaptive-method steps with a hyperbolic mirror map to add L1 sparsity bias while retaining stability.
K0EOhVw3B8.problem: Standard optimizers fail to encourage sparsity and keep training stable at once: adaptive optimizers have an implicit L-infinity bias favoring stability, but sparsity requires an L1 bias.
K0EOhVw3B8.method: Casts compositions of optimizer steps as non-commutative operators to analyze and combine their optimization geometries, yielding HORST, a modular optimizer. It inherits stability from adaptive methods and induces L1 sparsity bias through a hyperbolic mirror map.
K0EOhVw3B8.key_idea: Compose an adaptive step with a hyperbolic mirror-map step, treated as non-commutative operators, so the L-infinity stability geometry and the L1 sparsity geometry combine.
K0EOhVw3B8.evidence: Sparse training of transformers on both vision and language tasks, compared with AdamW baselines and the closely related HAM optimizer.
K0EOhVw3B8.claimed_gains: Consistently improves over AdamW baselines with the largest gains at higher sparsity and outperforms HAM in this regime; no numbers stated.

l9jTZzQJwR.one_liner: Schedules all-to-all exchanges and gradient all-reduce of a Ulysses-CP plus EP MoE block jointly to overlap communication with computation.
l9jTZzQJwR.problem: In MoE training with Ulysses context parallelism and expert parallelism, existing overlap methods largely optimize the AllToAll and AllReduce communication paths separately.
l9jTZzQJwR.method: An asymmetric scheduler coordinates the exchanges and computation under a common critical-path communication exposure (CCE) objective: forward A2A is split into point-to-point rounds overlapped with matrix multiplication, backward schedules ready weight-gradient tasks to overlap A2A, and AR runs on ready gradient slices between A2A exchanges. It is implemented as a scheduling layer in Megatron that preserves communication volume and training semantics.
l9jTZzQJwR.key_idea: Optimize forward A2A, backward A2A, and gradient AR together under one critical-path communication exposure objective, filling exposed time with ready weight-gradient and gradient-slice work.
l9jTZzQJwR.evidence: Block-level comparisons at 16K tokens on three public MoE families against Megatron and DeepSpeed-MoE, measured CCE, end-to-end loss trajectories, and multi-node evaluation on data-center GPUs.
l9jTZzQJwR.claimed_gains: Block-level speedups reach 1.2x against Megatron with gradient-reduce overlap and 1.7x against DeepSpeed-MoE at 16K tokens, and measured CCE falls by up to 67% relative to non-overlap Megatron.

qTScIebcYw.one_liner: Unified conditional diffusion LiDAR world model distilled into a four-step causal student for real-time generation, forecasting, and resimulation.
qTScIebcYw.problem: Reconstruction-based LiDAR simulators need lengthy per-scene optimization, while generative ones lack the consistency needed for long-horizon roll-outs.
qTScIebcYw.method: A fully attention-based tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences with different scanning patterns into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional diffusion teacher conditions on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally text. The teacher is distilled into a four-step autoregressive causal student with a rolling temporal K/V cache and a world-aligned spatial cache.
qTScIebcYw.key_idea: One conditional diffusion model switches among generation, forecasting, and resimulation by changing available scene evidence, then distills into a causal student with temporal K/V and spatial caches.
qTScIebcYw.evidence: Three evaluation protocols covering generation, forecasting, and resimulation, with a tokenizer that supports different sensors (remaining details cut off in the abstract).
qTScIebcYw.claimed_gains: Claims top results on most reported metrics across all three evaluation protocols, with real-time inference at 11 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

dOgxNVt2JF.one_liner: Learns a shared semantic frame with sparse coordinates reconstructing semantic displacements in LM representations while suppressing nuisance variation.
dOgxNVt2JF.problem: It is unclear whether semantic variation in language model representations is organized along recurring local directions that stay stable under meaning-preserving transformations.
dOgxNVt2JF.method: Proposes the Invariant Atom Hypothesis and learns a shared semantic frame plus sparse coordinates that reconstruct semantic displacements while suppressing nuisance variation. Anchor-dependent diagonal modulation adjusts atom strengths without sample-specific rotations.
dOgxNVt2JF.key_idea: Local semantic motion has preferred sparse coordinates along directions stable under meaning-preserving transformations, with anchor-dependent diagonal modulation scaling atom strengths instead of rotating them.
dOgxNVt2JF.evidence: Empirical analyses of semantic-nuisance separation, sparse reconstruction, direction reproducibility, causal effects on model predictions, generalization to unseen semantic neighborhoods and nuisance families, and stability under model modification; specific models and datasets are not stated.

3n6md5tUes.one_liner: Proves convex logit-space regularization, including label smoothing, induces logit clustering and aligns linear classifier weights with the LDA direction.
3n6md5tUes.problem: The mechanism by which label smoothing improves calibration and generalization in classification is under-explored.
3n6md5tUes.method: Analyzes a broad class of logit regularizers (convex penalties added directly in logit space) for linear classification, then studies a simple signal-plus-noise model to show the consequences of the induced bias.
3n6md5tUes.key_idea: Convex logit-space penalties cluster logits around finite per-sample targets, which for Gaussian data forces the weight vector to align exactly with the LDA direction.
3n6md5tUes.evidence: Theoretical proofs for linear classification (exact for Gaussian data, approximate for any distribution when logits are sufficiently clustered) and a signal-plus-noise model; no empirical benchmarks are mentioned.
3n6md5tUes.claimed_gains: Logit regularization halves the critical sample complexity, induces grokking in the small-noise limit, and makes generalization robust to noise.

r7fHCMzD12.one_liner: Identifies which concepts a diffusion model has unlearned, and how many, via spectral analysis of weight footprints.
r7fHCMzD12.problem: Attacks on unlearned diffusion models assume the erased concepts are known, but providers may not disclose which concepts were removed or how many.
r7fHCMzD12.method: TRACER applies lightweight spectral analysis of weight footprints to search large candidate vocabularies without generating or classifying images, and uses a footprint coverage objective to guide sequential discovery of multiple concepts. It estimates the count by detecting a sharp decline in candidate confidence, without labeled calibration examples.
r7fHCMzD12.key_idea: Rank candidate concepts by how well they account for the spectral footprint that unlearning left in the weights, discovering concepts sequentially until the footprint is covered.
r7fHCMzD12.evidence: Experiments across text-to-image and text-to-video backbones and diverse unlearning methods (details cut off in the provided abstract).

jMeylvhIoI.one_liner: Few-shot demonstration-guided RLVR that combines supervised and on-policy signals with decaying weights on 128 SFT demonstrations.
jMeylvhIoI.problem: RLVR struggles with sample efficiency on hard problems where correct rollouts are rare, and demonstration-guided RLVR via SFT needs a lot of costly data.
jMeylvhIoI.method: FEST uses only 128 demonstrations randomly selected from an SFT dataset. Three components are vital: a supervised signal, an on-policy signal, and decaying weights on the few-shot SFT data to prevent overfitting from multi-epoch training.
jMeylvhIoI.key_idea: Combine supervised and on-policy signals on a small demonstration set, with decaying loss weights on that set to prevent overfitting across multiple epochs.
jMeylvhIoI.evidence: Several benchmarks (not named in the abstract) comparing FEST with baselines in the few-shot setting.
jMeylvhIoI.claimed_gains: With only 128 randomly selected demonstrations, FEST outperforms baselines in the few-shot setting and matches baselines trained with orders of magnitude more SFT data.

eqdezLvlDF.one_liner: Orchestrates LLM agents guided by different decision theories via theory-guided training and consensus-first expert adaptation for personalized decisions.
eqdezLvlDF.problem: LLM agents for decision modeling lack theoretical grounding, show unstable reasoning, and give limited interpretability, and it is unclear which theory-guided agents to select or orchestrate for different tasks and personas.
eqdezLvlDF.method: L2AO has Theory-guided Agent Learning (TAL), which constructs and trains decision agents under different behavioral theories, and Consensus-First Expert Adaptation (CFEA), which coordinates the learned agents through a democratic AI mechanism that prioritizes cross-theory consensus. CFEA also adapts to task- and persona-specific differences.
eqdezLvlDF.key_idea: Treat diverse decision theories as complementary experts and combine their agents by prioritizing cross-theory consensus while adapting to task and persona differences.
eqdezLvlDF.evidence: Experiments on five real-world survey-based decision datasets (results cut off in the provided abstract).

wZEk6U3vds.one_liner: Benchmark of 4,084 ten-option questions on real longitudinal wearable data from 200 users, built with literature- and population-grounded questions.
wZEk6U3vds.problem: LLM reasoning over longitudinal wearable data is underexplored, and available benchmarks largely rely on synthetic or simulated signals.
wZEk6U3vds.method: WearableQA draws multiple-choice questions from wearable time series, blood biomarkers, and demographics of 200 real users with up to about 500 days of daily measurements, using 16 question types along data versus health reasoning and single versus cross-signal reasoning. Questions are built with a dual-grounding framework combining literature-grounded physiological findings with statistically validated population-grounded patterns.
wZEk6U3vds.key_idea: Dual-grounding question construction pairs literature-based physiological findings with statistically validated population patterns, applied to real wearable data with device noise and inter-individual variability.
wZEk6U3vds.evidence: Benchmark built from 200 real users' data; model evaluation results are cut off in the provided abstract.

fWKGpAYUxZ.one_liner: Synthesizes layer transformations at runtime by recursively recomposing a shared basis dictionary through input-conditioned states, decoupling depth from parameters.
fWKGpAYUxZ.problem: Deeper computation normally requires stacking more parameterized layers, which ties functional depth to parameter depth.
fWKGpAYUxZ.method: Recursive Basis Networks recursively recompose a shared basis dictionary through input-conditioned states, synthesizing heterogeneous transformations without layer-specific parameters. Depth becomes a runtime-controllable dimension while the transformation parameter budget stays fixed.
fWKGpAYUxZ.key_idea: Each step of depth builds a new transformation by recombining the same finite basis dictionary under input-conditioned states, so functional depth grows without new parameters.
fWKGpAYUxZ.evidence: Experiments across diverse approximation and representation-learning settings; specific datasets and models are not stated.
fWKGpAYUxZ.claimed_gains: Claims strong expressivity, parameter efficiency, and flexible depth scaling; no numbers stated.

akstqbtTKt.one_liner: VLA framework that distills privileged future observations into a latent reasoning chain usable from current observations only.
akstqbtTKt.problem: Existing VLA reasoning is externalized as verbal chains of thought or explicit predictive representations of future evolution, constrained to explicit formats or predefined semantic and temporal roles.
akstqbtTKt.method: ForeSense uses a Future-Conditioned Attention Bottleneck to pass future-observation information through an autoregressive latent chain, which is distilled into a current-only reasoner to form latent visual intuition. Detached Latent Curriculum (DeLaC) extends the chain gradually with stop-gradient on the existing latent prefix; a third design is cut off in the provided abstract.
akstqbtTKt.key_idea: Distill an autoregressive latent chain conditioned on future observations into a current-only reasoner, extending the chain step by step with stop-gradient on earlier latents to avoid collapse.
akstqbtTKt.evidence: not stated in the provided abstract, which is truncated before the experiments

EUuvOa0gGL.one_liner: Jointly generates molecular size, 2D topology, and local internal 3D geometry on a shared tree using a Bayesian Flow Network.
EUuvOa0gGL.problem: Most 3D molecule generators pre-sample molecular size, generate Cartesian coordinates, and often rely on equivariant architectures, while internal-coordinate methods need a known graph or autoregressive construction that may accumulate errors.
EUuvOa0gGL.method: TreeRef assigns topology and topology-dependent local 3D geometry to a variable-size tree, with RingRef nodes encoding ring closures and Null nodes letting size emerge from node occupancy. TreeRef-BFN, a Bayesian Flow Network with a standard Transformer backbone, jointly generates discrete variables and continuous local geometry, and masking alone supports variable-size structure-conditioned generation without retraining.
EUuvOa0gGL.key_idea: A tree representation with ring-closure and null nodes lets molecular size emerge from node occupancy, so a Transformer-based BFN needs no equivariance and conditions via masking.
EUuvOa0gGL.evidence: Empirical studies on unconditional, structure-conditioned, and property-conditioned 3D generation; datasets are not named in the visible abstract.
EUuvOa0gGL.claimed_gains: Claims strong chemical validity, molecular stability, and diversity, accurate local geometric distributions, fast sampling, and competitive property-conditioned generation; no numbers stated.

0kjAL88DFc.one_liner: Assesses degraded surveillance streams against a per-camera scene grammar estimated from that camera's own undistorted history.
0kjAL88DFc.problem: A single scalar quality score cannot say which observations in a surveillance scene remain dependable, such as whether a person was removed, a phantom added, or a parked vehicle made to look moving.
0kjAL88DFc.method: A camera scene grammar stores persistent anchors, class-conditioned occupancy, track continuity, and relation context from undistorted history. Comparing a stream with it yields three typed evidence channels (missing expected content, unsupported observations, inadmissible relations) plus a coverage mask, and a grammar-conditioned student amortizes the comparison using supervision from clean and degraded pairs without opinion scores.
0kjAL88DFc.key_idea: Compare the stream with the camera's own history-derived grammar to get typed evidence of missing, unsupported, and inadmissible content, with a coverage mask for where history cannot support judgment.
0kjAL88DFc.evidence: An exact error decomposition for ensemble consensus under shared generator bias, conditional monotonicity and stability guarantees, an identifiability limit, and a camera-disjoint evaluation protocol (results cut off in the abstract).

mEZIHlARHY.one_liner: Diagnostic environment replaying weeks of real news, market, and social-media streams to evaluate long-lived LLM agents that act sparsely.
mEZIHlARHY.problem: Existing long-horizon agent work usually assumes a static environment, so it misses unattended operation over days or weeks, acting at the right time, and adapting as the environment changes.
mEZIHlARHY.method: ReLiveGym has tasks of varying time sensitivity, reasoning intensity, and recurrence in which agents act sparsely over simulated weeks of chronologically replayed streams. The authors vary base models and harness design and also evaluate continuous learning from hindsight feedback.
mEZIHlARHY.key_idea: Chronologically replay real-world streams so agents must decide when to act, letting harness design (action timing) and hindsight-feedback learning be tested as separate axes.
mEZIHlARHY.evidence: Eight base language models evaluated across the long-lived tasks with different harness designs and hindsight-feedback learning.
mEZIHlARHY.claimed_gains: States that how agents determine when to act is an important harness-design axis and that the optimal design varies across tasks and sometimes across models; no numbers stated.

o6KoGVEyQH.one_liner: Selects useful theoretical samples for experimental chemistry data via Gaussian-mixture subdomain modeling and local KL-based iterative alignment.
o6KoGVEyQH.problem: Scarce, heterogeneous experimental data and abundant, subdomain-biased theoretical data cause distribution misalignment and negative transfer, and existing transfer and multi-fidelity methods assume global theory-experiment consistency.
o6KoGVEyQH.method: MDG-IS models experimental subdomains with a Gaussian Mixture Model and performs local KL-based alignment to iteratively extract a compact, well-aligned subset of theoretical data.
o6KoGVEyQH.key_idea: Fit a Gaussian mixture to experimental subdomains and iteratively keep only theoretical samples whose local distribution, measured by KL divergence, aligns with each subdomain.
o6KoGVEyQH.claimed_gains: Claims markedly reduced computational cost, mitigated negative transfer, and consistently improved prediction accuracy in real scenarios; no numbers stated.

fhIZw4hrrt.one_liner: Controls how a garment is worn in virtual try-on via draggable proxy point mappings routed through a Fold/ReFold attention branch.
fhIZw4hrrt.problem: Diffusion-based try-on offers limited control over wearing style: text instructions leave target positions ambiguous, and existing spatial interfaces restrict garment-part coverage or give insufficient control adherence.
fhIZw4hrrt.method: ProxyFit represents the wearing state with editable proxy point mappings from a flat garment to the body. An automated pipeline matches mesh-derived garment and person points and builds contrastive try-on pairs, and a proxy branch has Fold extract person-point features, attention retrieve local garment features, and ReFold write them back at the specified body locations.
fhIZw4hrrt.key_idea: Fold extracts person-point features, attention retrieves local garment features, and ReFold writes them back at user-specified body points, explicitly routing garment appearance to target locations.
fhIZw4hrrt.evidence: Experiments on point control (front opening, sleeve placement, hem placement, fit) and on standard virtual try-on.
fhIZw4hrrt.claimed_gains: 82.8% mean spatial control accuracy, exceeding WAW-style by 9.5 percentage points, and a 32.1% relative reduction in point-placement error (the comparison baseline is cut off in the abstract).

4dYWoCQ85a.one_liner: Uses language feedback to guide exploration and numerical rewards to drive optimization, with an on-policy experience pool for LLM RL.
4dYWoCQ85a.problem: Scalar-reward RL for LLMs discards textual rationale in rollouts, and naive reuse of text risks memorization from leaked solutions or behavior collapse from irrelevant context.
4dYWoCQ85a.method: LANPO separates the roles of feedback and uses a dynamically evolving experience pool built from on-policy rollouts. It applies Reward-Agnostic Reflection for intra-sample self-correction and Relevant Abstraction to distill lessons from inter-sample experiences.
4dYWoCQ85a.key_idea: Separate roles of feedback: language from an on-policy experience pool guides exploration through reward-agnostic reflection and relevant abstraction, while numerical rewards alone drive optimization.
4dYWoCQ85a.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and coding benchmarks with 7B and 14B models, compared against GRPO-trained baselines.
4dYWoCQ85a.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms strong GRPO-trained baselines for 7B and 14B models in zero-shot accuracy and further improves with feedback-augmented inference at test time; no other numbers stated.

jsD1puKzWX.one_liner: Gates news-augmented LLM forecasting with an Explainable Process Reward Model scoring causal, commonsense, and logic-consistent reflections.
jsD1puKzWX.problem: Existing LLM iterative forecasters generate reflections that only identify missing news categories, without causal reasoning about impact or plausibility checks, making the refinement loop prone to spurious correlations and slow convergence.
jsD1puKzWX.method: Introduces a reflection framework with three constraints: a causal chain linking missing news to prediction errors, a commonsense sanity check, and a logic consistency constraint against prior reflections. An Explainable Process Reward Model (EPRM) scores candidate news by expected error reduction and rational quality, and only candidates passing a quality gate are incorporated.
jsD1puKzWX.key_idea: Score candidate news jointly on expected error reduction and causal, commonsense, and logic quality with a trained process reward model, admitting only candidates that pass a quality gate.
jsD1puKzWX.evidence: Electricity, bitcoin, traffic, and exchange-rate benchmarks, plus automatic-judge and expert scores on causal, commonsense, and logic quality and usefulness.
jsD1puKzWX.claimed_gains: 10.5% average RMSE reduction over the unconstrained iterative baseline, and on bitcoin the spurious-item rate falls from 40.3% to 4.0%.

S5iafft0Rw.one_liner: Distills LLM-judge decision logic into a committee of executable Python programs, escalating low-confidence cases to an LLM.
S5iafft0Rw.problem: LLM-as-a-judge has high cost, inference latency, and opaque decisions, which undermine its scalability and reliability.
S5iafft0Rw.method: PAJAMA synthesizes programs as judges, aggregates their decisions into a joint verdict, and includes a fallback that escalates low-confidence cases to an LLM. Program outputs can also serve as routing signals and as labels for training a reward model.
S5iafft0Rw.key_idea: Replace per-sample LLM prompting with a committee of synthesized programs that score candidates directly, using program confidence to route uncertain cases back to an LLM judge.
S5iafft0Rw.evidence: Five datasets and eight model families, plus RewardBench for a reward model distilled from program verdicts.
S5iafft0Rw.claimed_gains: Programmatic judges match the performance of a 13B-size LLM judge at 47x higher throughput, and a reward model distilled from program verdicts outperforms one trained on a proprietary LLM's labels on RewardBench at two orders of magnitude lower API cost.

W52Hh99Iy6.one_liner: Evaluates driving world-action models by mapping video and action into a shared yaw and longitudinal-progress space to score consistency.
W52Hh99Iy6.problem: It is unclear whether the native action and imagined future of a driving world-action model describe compatible motion and respond together to changes in conditioning.
W52Hh99Iy6.method: Image-Action Consistency (IAC) maps video and action into a shared space of yaw and interval longitudinal progress using candidate-blind visual measurement with explicit observation coverage. It reports an Alignment Score (within-pair motion agreement), a Response Consistency Score (paired yaw responses to controlled condition changes), and a Grounding Score (geometric agreement with logged futures), and paired visual-motion targets are also used for training.
W52Hh99Iy6.key_idea: Measure motion from the generated video independently of the candidate and compare it with the predicted action in a shared yaw and progress space, reporting coverage alongside agreement.
W52Hh99Iy6.evidence: Held-out logged videos for visual progress estimation, a DriveWAM intervention protocol with 745 valid pairs, and fine-tuning comparisons on DriveWAM and WorldDrive measured by PDMS.
W52Hh99Iy6.claimed_gains: Visual progress estimates reach 90.1% tolerance accuracy at 88.2% coverage, response directions agree in 92.5% of pairs with detectable responses while only 49.5% of 745 valid pairs produce material action responses, and paired visual-motion targets improve PDMS by 1.54 points on DriveWAM and 1.00 point on WorldDrive over matched-budget action-only fine-tuning.

bxV8FvKGca.one_liner: Compresses per-example gradients for LLM influence functions using EK-FAC dimension reduction, PCA, and one-bit quantization.
bxV8FvKGca.problem: Reusing stored training gradients cuts influence-function cost, but storing full gradients is prohibitively expensive at LLM scale.
bxV8FvKGca.method: A worst-case analysis characterizes the optimal fixed-dimensional linear representation, which EOGP approximates by using EK-FAC to reduce gradient dimensionality, PCA within the retained subspace to learn compression directions, and one-bit quantization of the resulting coordinates so more coordinates fit a fixed storage budget.
bxV8FvKGca.key_idea: Learn compression directions by PCA inside an EK-FAC subspace, then quantize coordinates to one bit so a fixed storage budget holds more of them.
bxV8FvKGca.evidence: GPT-2 retraining-outcome prediction against compression baselines, and OLMo 2 SFT models from 1B to 32B parameters.
bxV8FvKGca.claimed_gains: On GPT-2, EOGP predicts retraining outcomes more accurately than the evaluated compression baselines using one-sixteenth of their per-example storage, and on OLMo 2 SFT models from 1B to 32B it remains competitive with baselines allocated over 100 times as much storage per example.

HaBr1WrToM.one_liner: Learns one score-aligned code per historical token shared across KV heads to find important tokens for CPU-offloaded KV-cache decoding.
HaBr1WrToM.problem: In long-context KV-cache offloading, sparse decoding needs a GPU-resident proxy to find important tokens, and existing projection-based proxies build a separate index per KV head, repeatedly storing and scanning related information.
HaBr1WrToM.method: JASP learns one joint code per historical token across KV heads, trained to preserve the query-key scores that determine token rankings rather than to reconstruct keys, with query-specific scoring and a per-KV-group selected token set. It adds GPU-driven selected-row retrieval and capacity-balanced CPU/GPU KV placement.
HaBr1WrToM.key_idea: Exploit shared query-conditioned attention-score structure across KV heads with a single code per token trained to preserve query-key scores, while keeping head-specific token selection.
HaBr1WrToM.evidence: An observation that KV heads share substantial attention-score structure across layers; evaluation results are cut off in the provided abstract.

KsdcIM2Jvb.one_liner: Schema-guided Mixture-of-Experts that aligns routing with cross-modal relation, reasoning demand, and temporal scope, trained with route-aware RL.
KsdcIM2Jvb.problem: Omni-modal models take video, audio, and text, but that does not ensure they use the right evidence, which matters in social video QA where answers hinge on gestures, vocal tone, temporal cues, or mismatch between speech and visuals.
KsdcIM2Jvb.method: A training-only cognitive schema factorizes each example by cross-modal relation, reasoning demand, and temporal scope to align global routing signatures during supervised fine-tuning. Route-aware reinforcement learning then jointly optimizes token generation and expert allocation with rewards for answer correctness, modality-consistent reasoning, and cognitive temporal grounding.
KsdcIM2Jvb.key_idea: A training-only schema aligns expert routing signatures with cross-modal relation, reasoning demand, and temporal scope, then RL jointly optimizes generation and expert allocation.
KsdcIM2Jvb.evidence: OmniSocialBench, a new diagnostic social video QA resource with 118 K structured training examples, grounded reasoning traces, schema labels, temporal evidence spans, and a manually verified evaluation split.
KsdcIM2Jvb.claimed_gains: Improves average accuracy on OmniSocialBench over the strongest proprietary baseline by 15.33 percentage points and over the strongest open-source omni baseline by 26.77 points.

RQkoZxYiTf.one_liner: Builds symbolic world models from reusable functional role prototypes and per-environment parameters so LLM agents transfer to new environments.
RQkoZxYiTf.problem: Symbolic or program-based world models still organize knowledge around environment-specific objects, which limits transfer to new environments with similar interaction structure.
RQkoZxYiTf.method: A teacher LLM extracts role prototypes and executable transition rules over role instances from interaction trajectories, plus a skill guiding the actor LLM. In a target world the actor uses the skill with current role assignments and parameter estimates, actively tests role-instance hypotheses when uncertain, and refines assignments and estimates online with no LLM parameter updates and fixed transition rules.
RQkoZxYiTf.key_idea: Describe object behavior with reusable role prototypes plus environment-specific parameter values, so transition rules stay fixed while role assignments and parameters are inferred online by active testing.
RQkoZxYiTf.evidence: Experiments on the MARS benchmark (results cut off in the provided abstract).

k5F1OZ8Pqs.one_liner: Assigns turn-level credit in RL-based multi-turn jailbreaking using leave-one-turn-out semantic masking, and reuses the signal for defense alignment.
k5F1OZ8Pqs.problem: Training-based multi-turn jailbreak methods use coarse trajectory-level outcome signals broadcast to every turn, over-rewarding redundant turns in successful trajectories and under-crediting useful intermediate turns in failed ones.
k5F1OZ8Pqs.method: TRACE estimates turn-level contributions in successful trajectories via leave-one-turn-out semantic masking, and for failed ones assigns penalties from prompt harmfulness and semantic relevance plus a local refusal-aware penalty. The attack-side credit signal is reused for multi-turn defense alignment.
k5F1OZ8Pqs.key_idea: Credit each turn by how much masking it semantically changes the outcome in successes, and penalize failed turns by harmfulness, relevance, and local refusal.
k5F1OZ8Pqs.evidence: Experiments on open-source and closed-source target models (details cut off in the abstract), motivated by an analysis finding turn contributions are non-uniform, phase-dependent, and target-specific.
k5F1OZ8Pqs.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after claiming the strongest overall results on open-source and closed-source targets)

EnLqDyNpC6.one_liner: Agentic evidence-diagnosis-revision loop that builds articulated digital twins with accurate geometry, collision proxies, and fitted physical parameters.
EnLqDyNpC6.problem: Visually plausible articulated assets may still fail during contact interactions or exhibit inaccurate motion.
EnLqDyNpC6.method: An agent drives an evidence-diagnosis-revision loop on a shared editable representation, selecting measurements and edits from quantitative feedback while numerical tools execute and validate updates. It reconstructs articulated geometry from images, repairs collision proxies by task-aware local repartitioning before fidelity-constrained compression, then fits response models from passive-response videos using simulation residuals.
EnLqDyNpC6.key_idea: An agent selects measurements and model edits from quantitative simulation residuals on a shared editable representation, while numerical tools validate each update.
EnLqDyNpC6.evidence: Experiments on geometric reconstruction against baselines, interaction with simpler collision proxies, and reproduction of held-out physical responses versus direct parameter inference.
EnLqDyNpC6.claimed_gains: Claims improved geometric reconstruction over baselines, more reliable interaction with simpler collision proxies, and better reproduction of held-out physical responses than direct parameter inference; no numbers stated.

H8jAz17C2s.one_liner: Extends multimodal emotion recognition into an agent loop of perception, understanding, planning and response, with model, dataset and benchmark.
H8jAz17C2s.problem: Multimodal emotion recognition stays perception-centric, so recognizing an emotion does not let an agent understand context, plan support or respond effectively.
H8jAz17C2s.method: EQ-MER is a sub-1B perception model built on a Perception-to-Cognition (P2C) Bridge with two-stage training, and EQ-Dataset has 30,664 records covering social reasoning, supportive response and emotional reasoning. EQ-Agentic couples multitask SFT with single-reward, EQ-Judge-guided agentic policy optimization for UNDERSTAND-PLAN-RESPONSE decisions, and EQ-Harness supplies the runtime.
H8jAz17C2s.key_idea: Initialize an agent from a small emotion-perception model and train UNDERSTAND-PLAN-RESPONSE decisions with SFT plus policy optimization guided by a single EQ-Judge reward.
H8jAz17C2s.evidence: Nine-dataset MER-UniBench for perception and a three-axis EQ-UniBench for agentic emotional intelligence (the abstract is truncated before the agentic results).
H8jAz17C2s.claimed_gains: EQ-MER reaches an 82.22% macro score on the nine-dataset MER-UniBench.

UMrkir8IPe.one_liner: Unifies motion generation tasks as masking patterns, using a masked motion tokenizer and an observation-aware latent flow-matching generator.
UMrkir8IPe.problem: Motion generation methods are built for individual tasks such as text-to-motion, pose-conditioned generation and trajectory control, with no unified framework over a common representation.
UMrkir8IPe.method: Treats each motion condition as an observation pattern, that is a masking strategy over the motion sequence. Three-stage training learns a masked motion tokenizer, refines its reconstruction on clean motions, and trains a conditional flow-matching generator in latent space, with an observation map and observation loss preserving the given conditions.
UMrkir8IPe.key_idea: Formulate each motion condition as a mask over the sequence, learn one masked tokenizer for full and partial motions, and generate with flow matching under an observation loss.
UMrkir8IPe.evidence: Experiments are not described in the visible abstract, which is truncated before the results.

bDk97oNoCj.one_liner: Controlled study splits the MLLM vision encoder into visual prior, dedicated capacity, and placement, tested at matched lifetime compute.
bDk97oNoCj.problem: How multimodal LLMs should process images is unsettled, and published models differ in data, backbone, and compute, so the roles of separate encoder pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and fusion placement are confounded.
bDk97oNoCj.method: The authors train 1.7B-8B multimodal LLMs from scratch on common data and compare variants that keep or drop a visual prior from separate pretraining, dedicated vision-only capacity, and the placement of that capacity before the backbone (pre-fusion) or inside it (in-fusion), evaluating at matched lifetime compute.
bDk97oNoCj.key_idea: Decompose the vision encoder into three separately ablated choices (separate pretraining, dedicated capacity, pre- versus in-fusion placement) under matched lifetime compute.
bDk97oNoCj.evidence: Controlled from-scratch training of 1.7B-8B multimodal LLMs on common data, evaluated on visual question answering and language benchmarks; an encoder trained from scratch matches same-data pretrained encoders, and encoder-free models trail on visual understanding.

HSM7JAmwVh.one_liner: Builds multi-agent reward signals from task-level behavioral tests via return functions and preference-based return-to-reward decomposition.
HSM7JAmwVh.problem: Dense rewards in MARL need task-specific engineering, while sparse rewards give too little guidance for coordination.
HSM7JAmwVh.method: TdMARL adapts Test-Driven RL to the multi-agent setting by building return functions from task-level evaluations and deriving per-step rewards. It adds MARL-specific data sampling and preference-evaluation mechanisms and a soft uniform prior for stable return-to-reward decomposition.
HSM7JAmwVh.key_idea: Treat task-level behavioral requirements as tests that define returns, then decompose returns into per-step rewards with preference learning and a soft uniform prior.
HSM7JAmwVh.evidence: A theoretical bound on test-failure probability under test separation and policy realizability, plus experiments across dense-reward, sparse-reward, and sparse-reward-with-auxiliary settings.

hXHhXyZMor.one_liner: Benchmark that trains laundered, unlaundered, and filler-only models from a shared checkpoint to test whether data laundering evades provenance detection.
hXHhXyZMor.problem: No evaluation protocol separates whether a provenance detector is underpowered, laundering succeeded, or the model failed to learn from rewritten data.
hXHhXyZMor.method: LaunderBench trains three update-matched models from a shared checkpoint (on rewrites, on originals, and on filler text only) and audits all three on the original documents, under three criteria: baseline detector auditability, audit evasion efficacy, and source utility viability.
hXHhXyZMor.key_idea: Compare update-matched laundered, unlaundered, and filler-only models audited on original documents to separate evasion from detector weakness and from learning.
hXHhXyZMor.evidence: Pythia-1.4B across 4 data corpora and 9 rewriting methods, varying training exposure and source-token quota, with supplementary experiments across model scales and architectures.

LRvOxy0Auj.one_liner: Wraps heterogeneous robot policies as agentic skills with capability-aware routing and a Memory Bridge for policy handoffs.
LRvOxy0Auj.problem: Long-horizon robot tasks need several complementary policies, but capability boundaries are uncertain and handoffs cause distribution mismatch, which planners assuming homogeneous, predefined skills do not handle.
LRvOxy0Auj.method: RoboHarness encapsulates VLAs, world-action models, RL policies, and TAMP planners as reusable agentic skills and adds understanding, memory, and evolution skills for capability-aware task decomposition and policy routing. Memory Bridge is a plug-in policy-chaining mechanism for transitions between heterogeneous policies without joint retraining.
LRvOxy0Auj.key_idea: Route tasks to heterogeneous policies via capability-aware skills with memory, and chain policies with a plug-in Memory Bridge that avoids joint retraining.
LRvOxy0Auj.evidence: Five public benchmarks, 500 customized tasks across 10 classes, and 135 real-robot trials.
LRvOxy0Auj.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports substantial gains in long-horizon and memory-dependent tasks without numbers)

LxraZd4JER.one_liner: Randomized-smoothing first-order algorithm that finds Goldstein approximate second-order stationary points of L-smooth functions.
LxraZd4JER.problem: The abstract states no specific gap; it targets computing Goldstein approximate second-order stationary points of structured nonsmooth nonconvex functions using first-order oracles.
LxraZd4JER.method: A randomized first-order algorithm built on randomized smoothing computes Goldstein approximate second-order stationary points of L-smooth functions. It extends to weakly convex functions via reduction to their Moreau envelopes and to bilevel problems with L-smooth or weakly convex hyperobjectives.
LxraZd4JER.key_idea: Use randomized smoothing to find Goldstein second-order stationary points of L-smooth functions from first-order oracle calls, and reduce weakly convex functions to their Moreau envelopes.
LxraZd4JER.evidence: Oracle-complexity analysis stated in the abstract; no experiments are described.
LxraZd4JER.claimed_gains: Oracle complexity of O~(n^2/eps^9 + n^3/eps^7), where n is the input dimension and eps is the common tolerance.

RoWXO7T48T.one_liner: Dual reversed rolling-shutter-with-global-reset capture with row-adaptive alignment and a hallucination module for HDR photosequencing.
RoWXO7T48T.problem: Rolling shutter with global reset (RSGR) reduces capture speed and compresses dynamic range, and rolling-shutter effects cause geometric distortion and motion artifacts in mobile CMOS photography.
RoWXO7T48T.method: A dual reversed scanning setup uses both RSGR and inverted RSGR views with synchronized complementary exposures. The network performs row-adaptive feature alignment, then a hallucination module with a correlation-guided mix-attention block recovers missing details, and a coaxial imaging system collects a real-world dataset.
RoWXO7T48T.key_idea: Capture complementary RSGR and inverted-RSGR exposures so rows balance dynamic range, then align row-wise features and fuse them with correlation-guided attention.
RoWXO7T48T.evidence: Experiments on numerical simulation and a real-world dataset from a coaxial imaging system; datasets and metrics are not named in the visible abstract.

baL5vR9j6k.one_liner: Importance-weighted conditional VAE with an MMD penalty aligning train and test representation marginals for domain-adaptive conditional generation.
baL5vR9j6k.problem: Generative models degrade when training and testing distributions differ, and existing domain adaptation assumes covariate or label shift, which can be restrictive under substantial domain shift.
baL5vR9j6k.method: IWCAE assumes a representation under which the conditional response distribution is invariant across domains and learns it with an importance-weighted conditional likelihood objective plus an MMD penalty aligning marginal representation distributions. A sampling-importance-resampling procedure gives approximate predictive sampling when the conditional latent prior is hard to sample.
baL5vR9j6k.key_idea: Align marginal representation distributions across domains with an MMD penalty while training the conditional response model with an importance-weighted likelihood.
baL5vR9j6k.evidence: An asymptotic validity result for the sampling procedure and experiments on three medical datasets.

VXb6iC5X71.one_liner: Closed-form Householder rotations aligning the leading activation eigenspace with the constant-group subspace of asymmetric grouped INT4 quantizers.
VXb6iC5X71.problem: Smaller activation outliers do not necessarily mean better low-bit quantization; what matters is how activations align with the quantizer.
VXb6iC5X71.method: PrismQuant formulates rotation design as a Ky Fan trace maximization with a provably optimal closed-form solution, built from compact Householder transformations in compact-WY form for gradient-free construction at foldable and online sites. A predictive range law links unaligned activation energy and group size to quantization-relevant variation.
VXb6iC5X71.key_idea: Rotates activations so the dominant eigenspace falls in the group-constant subspace that the quantizer's affine offsets already represent, by solving a Ky Fan trace maximization.
VXb6iC5X71.evidence: W4A4KV4 experiments on Llama, Qwen, and Mistral models up to 70B parameters and a 30B mixture-of-experts model, plus a deployment study on Llama-3.1-8B.
VXb6iC5X71.claimed_gains: On Llama-3.1-70B, 3.85 perplexity and 72.46% average zero-shot accuracy, 0.22 percentage points below full precision; on Llama-3.1-8B, 1.51x prefill and 1.22x CUDA Graph decode speedups over matched FP16 baselines.

Ma4fnHVnsT.one_liner: Study of GNN depth degradation on Minesweeper using a mean-field reference model and tests of width and weight decay.
Ma4fnHVnsT.problem: Depth degradation in GNNs, a performance drop with more layers, could reflect optimization failure, poor generalization, or representation collapse, and over-smoothing diagnostics alone do not settle which.
Ma4fnHVnsT.method: The paper derives a mean-field scheme that iteratively updates node label probabilities on Minesweeper, then tests when learned GCNs can recover its inductive biases (low-dimensional communication and recurrence) while varying width, weight decay, and depth, and compares hidden rank and Dirichlet energy.
Ma4fnHVnsT.key_idea: Combining sufficient width with weight decay lets an unrestricted GCN match gains at moderate depths, associated with lower-rank message maps; over-smoothing diagnostics alone do not explain depth degradation.
Ma4fnHVnsT.evidence: Minesweeper and City-Networks node-classification experiments with a mean-field scheme and learned GCNs of varying depth, width, and weight decay.
Ma4fnHVnsT.claimed_gains: The mean-field scheme reaches 99.9% test ROC-AUC on Minesweeper; no other numbers stated.

xmxQbRxMjM.one_liner: GRASP detects multivariate time-series anomalies with flow matching along a closed-form graph-spectral probability path.
xmxQbRxMjM.problem: Standard flow matching uses linear probability paths that ignore dependencies among variables, which misaligns with structured multivariate time-series distributions.
xmxQbRxMjM.method: GRASP builds the probability path by minimizing a fixed-endpoint action of kinetic energy plus graph Dirichlet energy, giving a closed form based on graph-frequency-dependent hyperbolic interpolation. A velocity predictor trained on normal data scores anomalies with weighted velocity discrepancies aggregated over source samples, flow times, and graph frequencies.
xmxQbRxMjM.key_idea: Replace the linear flow-matching path with the minimizer of kinetic plus graph Dirichlet energy, yielding graph-frequency-dependent hyperbolic interpolation, and score anomalies by velocity discrepancy.
xmxQbRxMjM.evidence: Theory showing invariance to the Laplacian eigenbasis choice and a decomposition of the expected oracle anomaly score into bounded endpoint uncertainty and graph-frequency-weighted Fisher discrepancy; experiments on four benchmarks.

l0kVqpzUOn.one_liner: Sets a per-prompt DPO beta from KKT conditions, proportional to reward standard deviation under the reference model.
l0kVqpzUOn.problem: DPO uses one fixed beta across prompts, and existing dynamic-beta methods rely on method-specific signals rather than deriving beta from the optimization problem.
l0kVqpzUOn.method: The paper formulates a per-prompt KL-constrained problem and shows the optimal multiplier is the product of the reference-model reward standard deviation and a dimensionless factor set by the standardized reward distribution and the KL budget. KKT-DPO approximates relative reward standard deviations from reference-policy samples scored by policy-to-reference log-ratios under a lagged policy snapshot, and uses a beta tuned for vanilla DPO as the anchor.
l0kVqpzUOn.key_idea: Scale each prompt's beta in proportion to its estimated reference-model reward standard deviation, anchored by the beta tuned for vanilla DPO.
l0kVqpzUOn.evidence: Derivation of the optimal per-prompt multiplier through KKT conditions; the experimental datasets and models are not visible in the truncated abstract.

FPFrQsrjP9.one_liner: Finds predictive-selective representation subspaces by contrasting Fisher information across semantic-preserving and semantic-changing neighborhoods via a generalized eigenproblem.
FPFrQsrjP9.problem: Euclidean displacement in representation space does not track predictive change, since comparable displacements can cause very different prediction shifts while semantic-preserving transformations move representations substantially.
FPFrQsrjP9.method: Fisher-IRG uses the local Fisher quadratic form and its predictive KL interpretation to measure representation directions. Contrasting Fisher information across semantic-preserving and semantic-changing neighborhoods yields predictive-selective subspaces through an efficient generalized eigenvalue procedure.
FPFrQsrjP9.key_idea: Select directions with high Fisher information in semantic-changing neighborhoods relative to semantic-preserving ones by solving a generalized eigenvalue problem.
FPFrQsrjP9.evidence: Language and vision models compared with covariance-based discovery on predictive selectivity and Grassmann reproducibility, plus representation interventions, held-out semantic discrimination, natural language inference data, and corruption-based visual retrieval.
FPFrQsrjP9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says stronger predictive selectivity and generally greater Grassmann reproducibility than covariance-based discovery, without numbers)

5ZR8q8uINE.one_liner: DistriVoting splits per-query confidence distributions with a Gaussian mixture and filters votes; SelfStepConf sharpens separation using step-level confidence.
5ZR8q8uINE.problem: Test-time scaling for reasoning models selects answers by voting, but the relative structure of each query's confidence distribution has not been used to guide answer selection.
5ZR8q8uINE.method: DistriVoting decomposes the mixed confidence distribution into higher- and lower-mean components with a Gaussian Mixture Model and applies a reject filter that uses the lower-mean component as counter-evidence. SelfStepConf uses step-level confidence to dynamically adjust inference and increase the separation between the two components.
5ZR8q8uINE.key_idea: Model each query's confidence distribution as a two-component Gaussian mixture, use the low-mean component to reject candidates, and widen separation via step-level confidence.
5ZR8q8uINE.claimed_gains: The abstract says the method outperforms prior approaches across 16 models and 5 benchmarks, with no numeric gains stated.

BT1csW3NRw.one_liner: Neural codec decoders regenerate partials above a bitrate-dependent band edge toward 12-TET harmonics, following the fine-tuning corpus.
BT1csW3NRw.problem: Neural synthesis pulls output tuning toward 12-TET, but it is unclear where inside a neural audio codec this happens and how it distorts pitch measurement.
BT1csW3NRw.method: Measures tuning of transmitted and invented partials around the codec band edge and runs a causal intervention that fine-tunes only EnCodec's decoder on retuned corpora so every arm reads bit-identical tokens. Compares against classical codecs and against a pitch estimator that fits across the edge.
BT1csW3NRw.key_idea: Decoders transmit lower partials and invent upper partials above a band edge that land on the nearest 12-TET harmonic ladder, set by the fine-tuning corpus.
BT1csW3NRw.evidence: Measurements on twenty-four stimuli and eleven measurable neural conditions spanning two codec families, plus a decoder-only fine-tuning intervention on EnCodec.
BT1csW3NRw.claimed_gains: No performance gain is claimed; headline findings are a median 4.37-cent displacement over twenty-four stimuli, a 33-cent corpus retuning moving the decoder grid by 32.7 +/- 2.8 cents, and six of eleven neural conditions showing the effect, four by more than five cents.

oGYbb3htR7.one_liner: gamma-BIFR generalizes DP-lambdaCGD and banded inverse square root factorizations for memory-efficient correlated-noise DP training.
oGYbb3htR7.problem: DP-lambdaCGD is memory-efficient with a one-step noise buffer but gains little utility, while banded inverse square root (BISR) is asymptotically optimal at large bandwidth but performs poorly at low bandwidth.
oGYbb3htR7.method: Introduces gamma-BIFR, a unified generalization of both banded inverse factorizations, targeting the low-memory, low-bandwidth regime of multi-epoch private training with correlated noise.
oGYbb3htR7.key_idea: A single banded inverse factorization that generalizes both DP-lambdaCGD and BISR, bridging their low- and high-bandwidth regimes.
oGYbb3htR7.evidence: Evaluated by RMSE, amplified RMSE, and private training performance, with tighter theoretical guarantees on multi-participation error; datasets and models are not stated in the visible abstract.
oGYbb3htR7.claimed_gains: In the low-memory, low-bandwidth regime it improves RMSE, amplified RMSE, and private training performance with tighter multi-participation error guarantees, with no numbers stated.

OLQtyzPpTT.one_liner: DELTA locates knowledge-concerned neurons in vision LLMs via decoupled attribution and edits them within an approximate null space.
OLQtyzPpTT.problem: Text-only locate-then-edit localization does not transfer to multimodal knowledge editing because knowledge encoded in vision LLMs differs from that in text-only LLMs.
OLQtyzPpTT.method: DELTA identifies candidate layers by tracing cross-modal fusion, feed-forward engagement, and activation traceability, then localizes neurons with decoupled attribution scores and visual filtering. Updates constrain parameter changes toward an approximate null space and perturb visual embeddings, with no auxiliary editor optimization.
OLQtyzPpTT.key_idea: Neuron-level locate-then-edit using decoupled vision-text attribution scores, with parameter updates constrained toward an approximate null space to preserve unrelated knowledge.
OLQtyzPpTT.evidence: Experiments reported across reliability, locality, and generality against existing knowledge editing approaches; the abstract is cut off before further details.

GDcoivauZY.one_liner: GARNET reranks Lean premise candidates by expanding retrieval anchors along Mathlib dependency-graph neighborhoods.
GDcoivauZY.problem: Existing premise retrievers match a natural-language query or local proof state directly and ignore structural relationships in the library's dependency graph.
GDcoivauZY.method: GARNET expands query- and state-conditioned anchor sets along local dependency neighborhoods and reranks candidates by combining direct retrieval evidence with structural context.
GDcoivauZY.key_idea: Expand query- and state-conditioned anchors along local dependency-graph neighborhoods, then rerank by direct retrieval evidence plus structural context.
GDcoivauZY.evidence: Retrieval benchmarks on Mathlib 4.28 and Lean Workbook, and an LLM proving agent for proof-sketch completion on a curated 60-theorem subset of ProofNet-Verified.
GDcoivauZY.claimed_gains: R@20 improves by over 20 absolute points on Mathlib 4.28, and in the proving agent it reaches 77.7 +/- 3.0% mean single-attempt accuracy and 88.3% pass@5 on the 60-theorem subset.

wzNZsBAbaD.one_liner: Reinforcement learning optimizes binder-generator denoising transitions using AlphaFold3 interface confidence as the reward.
wzNZsBAbaD.problem: Likelihood-trained protein binder generators consider binding mainly during inference-time candidate filtering rather than in their training objective.
wzNZsBAbaD.method: BindGRPO casts the target-conditioned denoising sampler as a Markov decision process with tractable Gaussian policy transitions. It post-trains the generator using AlphaFold3 interface confidence for co-designed sequences without requiring experimentally determined target-binder complexes.
wzNZsBAbaD.key_idea: Treat denoising steps as Gaussian policy transitions and optimize them with predicted target-binder interface confidence rewards.
wzNZsBAbaD.evidence: Evaluation uses the Cao benchmark, an independent AlphaFold2 evaluator, and multiple success thresholds.
wzNZsBAbaD.claimed_gains: BindGRPO increases in-silico success from 24.4% to 36.7%, a 1.51× gain over the same generator before reinforcement-learning fine-tuning.

Vwqd2ouPnR.one_liner: Text-guided support consensus distills into target prototypes for query-only spectral detection in unseen scenes.
Vwqd2ouPnR.problem: Varying target spectra and backgrounds limit transfer of fixed priors and labeled-scene target knowledge to open scenes.
Vwqd2ouPnR.method: TCPL matches local spectral-spatial support neighborhoods with query pixels using asymmetric text guidance and aggregates predictions across supports. Detection supervision and distillation transfer this consensus into a prototype bank and target anchor for query-only inference.
Vwqd2ouPnR.key_idea: Distill consensus across text-guided support-conditioned predictions into learned prototypes and a target anchor.
Vwqd2ouPnR.evidence: The paper constructs three datasets with pixel-level target annotations and a unified open-scene evaluation setting.

SUxaNjKUP8.one_liner: Attacker-defender co-evolution with historical opponent populations and verified demonstrations trains defenses against adaptive indirect prompt injection.
SUxaNjKUP8.problem: Defenses trained against fixed indirect prompt injections may fail when attackers adapt to tool-using agents' behavior.
SUxaNjKUP8.method: CoER models interleaved tool use and repeated adaptive injections as a general-sum Markov game. Bilateral adversarial reinforcement learning mixes current and historical opponents, then population attackers challenge teacher agents to obtain demonstrations verified for safety and task completion.
SUxaNjKUP8.key_idea: Co-train adaptive attackers and defenders against historical opponent populations, then refine behavior using jointly safety- and completion-verified demonstrations.

kitAxeqcb1.one_liner: Shared gated KV caches across reasoning loops reduce looped-transformer memory while preserving local per-loop context.
kitAxeqcb1.problem: Looped language models retain KV caches across iterations, causing memory consumption to grow with reasoning depth.
kitAxeqcb1.method: MELT maintains a shared KV cache per layer across loops and per-loop caches within a small sliding window, updating the shared cache through learned gating. Chunk-wise training aligns training with inference when adapting pretrained Ouro parameters.
kitAxeqcb1.key_idea: Share a gated layer-level KV cache across loops while retaining separate loop-specific caches only in a small sliding window.
kitAxeqcb1.evidence: Models fine-tuned from Ouro are compared with the original Ouro models and standard language models of comparable size for performance and memory use.

GUQxdke81L.one_liner: Gyro-homomorphic projections and Busemann similarity construct attention intrinsically in Lorentz hyperbolic space.
GUQxdke81L.problem: Attention mechanisms lack a principled construction that faithfully respects hyperbolic geometry for hierarchical data.
GUQxdke81L.method: HBformer uses gyro-homomorphisms for query and value updates and Lorentz Busemann functions for curvature-aware attention scores. A Lorentz-to-Euclidean fully connected layer supplies tangent-space keys required by the similarity function.
GUQxdke81L.key_idea: Combine Lorentz gyro-homomorphic query-value maps with Busemann attention scores and tangent-space keys.
GUQxdke81L.evidence: Experiments compare Euclidean and hyperbolic baselines on graph benchmarks, large-scale node property prediction, and semi-supervised image and text classification.

9Xbi0b1Dg7.one_liner: Collaborative preference completion and history-conditioned Riemannian flow matching generate content distributions from sparse user behavior.
9Xbi0b1Dg7.problem: Sparse user behavior leaves uncertainty about both desired content and how generation probabilities should spread across user interests.
9Xbi0b1Dg7.method: The framework uses cross-user behavioral patterns to complete individual preference distributions. Source-distribution modeling and history-conditioned Riemannian flow matching allocate semantic latent probability mass, which a decoder converts directly into content without explicit prompts.
9Xbi0b1Dg7.key_idea: Complete sparse preference distributions using collaborative behavior, then sample semantic latents through history-conditioned Riemannian flow matching.
9Xbi0b1Dg7.evidence: Experiments use short-video user interaction benchmarks with textual descriptions as generation targets.

u1QwiJ3cZL.one_liner: Attack-operation valuation schedules expensive ensemble updates early, followed by base updates, to allocate adversarial attack computation.
u1QwiJ3cZL.problem: Ensemble attacks repeatedly apply costly updates without accounting for how their final transferability benefit varies along the attack trajectory.
u1QwiJ3cZL.method: Attack Operation Value compares final transfer effects of method-specific and base ensemble updates starting from the same attack state. Temporal Ensemble Scheduling uses stage-dependent update allocation, motivated by early expensive updates followed by sufficient base optimization.
u1QwiJ3cZL.key_idea: Measure update value at a given attack state and schedule expensive versus base ensemble updates across the trajectory.
u1QwiJ3cZL.evidence: Fixed-compute-budget experiments examine stage-dependent update returns and the effect of allocating expensive updates early in ensemble attacks.

cMNaCZyQdB.one_liner: Token-adaptive latent recurrence lets difficult diffusion-language-model positions receive extra computation while resolved tokens become discrete context.
cMNaCZyQdB.problem: Uniform denoising depth mismatches token difficulty and contributes to diffusion language models' quality gap against autoregressive models.
cMNaCZyQdB.method: ALoDLM recurrently refines latent token representations, committing ready tokens as discrete context while unresolved tokens receive additional passes. It treats token-wise computation schedules as latent variables and derives a conditional negative evidence lower bound for joint training.
cMNaCZyQdB.key_idea: Commit resolved tokens as discrete context while recurrently refining unresolved latent states under learned token-wise computation schedules.
cMNaCZyQdB.evidence: Experiments evaluate 1.7B and 8B models across eleven benchmarks against diffusion language models and corresponding autoregressive baselines.

5n4xeaG7bM.one_liner: Hessian-derived curvature weights modify trellis branch costs to quantize language-model weights without rotation.
5n4xeaG7bM.problem: Existing two-bit quantizers use curvature only between coding blocks and require rotations that must be undone during decoding.
5n4xeaG7bM.method: CurveTQ inserts diagonal weights from the Hessian's LDL factorization into the Viterbi branch metric. This makes trellis search account for within-block curvature in the native weight basis, replacing the role of rotation.
5n4xeaG7bM.key_idea: Weight Viterbi branch distances by Hessian LDL diagonal entries to perform curvature-aware trellis search in the native basis.
5n4xeaG7bM.evidence: Experiments on three models compare weighted native-basis search with full-dimension randomized Hadamard rotation and assess weighting after rotation.
5n4xeaG7bM.claimed_gains: Weighted native search matches the baselines' rotation to within about one point of downstream accuracy.

l6Zp492Ag2.one_liner: Nuisance-canceling measurement groups expose information and local-exchange barriers in batch experimental design.
l6Zp492Ag2.problem: Greedy and small-exchange measurement selection can miss groups whose target information appears only when nuisance components jointly cancel.
